# aikido_container_clone (Resource)

Scan additional tags of an existing container using separate clones, each with its own tag filter. The source container must belong to a connected registry.

Cloud-discovered containers, public images and uploaded SBOMs cannot be cloned.

## Basic usage

Each clone starts active, and Aikido requests a scan immediately. A wildcard selects one matching image, not every matching tag.

Replace `12345` with your source container's ID. Use [`aikido_containers`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/AikidoTerraform/aikido/latest/docs/data-sources/containers) to find it and [`aikido_container`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/AikidoTerraform/aikido/latest/docs/resources/container) to configure its own tag filter.

```terraform
# Add two tag filters to existing container 12345.
# The source container keeps its own tag filter.
resource "aikido_container_clone" "api" {
  for_each = toset(["staging-*", "semver-production"])

  source_container_id = 12345
  tag_filter          = each.value
}
```

## Optional settings

Cloning does not copy labels, sensitivity or connectivity from the source container. Manage these settings and activation with an `aikido_container` using the clone's ID. Omit `tag_filter` to keep the clone's filter.

```terraform
resource "aikido_container" "api_clones" {
  for_each = aikido_container_clone.api

  id          = each.value.id
  active      = true
  sensitivity = "sensitive"
  labels      = ["api"]
}
```

## Replacement and destroy

> **Warning:** Removing this resource deactivates the clone but does not delete it. Aikido still reserves its tag filter, so adding the same tag back will fail.

Changing `source_container_id` or `tag_filter` also replaces the clone, leaving the old clone inactive. Reverting to a previously used tag filter or forcing replacement with the same filter will fail for the same reason.

To resume scanning without importing, configure an `aikido_container` with the existing clone's ID and `active = true`. If you also restore `aikido_container_clone` to the configuration, import it before applying. Import alone does not reactivate it.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `source_container_id` (Number) Aikido container ID of the existing registry container to clone. Changing it replaces the clone.
- `tag_filter` (String) Tag filter deciding which image the clone scans. Supports * wildcards, for example prod-*, and the special value semver-production. Must not be empty or have surrounding whitespace. Changing it replaces the clone. Aikido rejects a tag already used by the source or another clone of the same image in the same registry, including inactive containers.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Aikido container ID of the clone.

## Import existing clones

Import a clone created in Aikido, including through the UI, using `<source_container_id>:<clone_id>`. Configure `source_container_id` and `tag_filter` to match the existing clone before importing.

Find the clone's ID in Aikido or with the `aikido_containers` data source, filtering by name, registry ID and tag filter. For registries spanning multiple regions, confirm that you selected the correct clone.

For the `staging-*` instance in the basic example, use [`terraform import`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import):

```shell
# Import the existing staging-* clone (12399) of source container 12345.
terraform import 'aikido_container_clone.api["staging-*"]' 12345:12399
```
